content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Matthew Mejia (E034), requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory has two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin only if role owns system. Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist, Analyst doesn't own it, so write is max for full-time. Approve write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. The security DB says contractor with basic training max read. Write requires advanced training, so capped to read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training.

As the Approver, I need to make a final decision. The two notes conflict on employment type. The safer/more restrictive approach: contractor with basic training maxes at read. Full time maxes at write. Given the conflict, the conservative decision is to grant read (the lower of the two), which satisfies the security note.

Policy: If requested level is above maximum, grant maximum. If conflicting info, choose the more restrictive interpretation. Read is at or below requested write.

So submit decision: read.
